appraisal_events.evidence: « son visage respirait la souffrance et la haine » ; « Il passait la plus grande partie de son temps à envoyer à sa maîtresse des lettres et des dépêches » ; « Dis-moi ce que j'ai fait de mal. Je suis prêt à reconnaître mes torts » ; « c'est presque toujours le front soucieux et bien souvent les mains vides que je voyais Saint-Loup revenir de la poste où, seul de tout l'hôtel avec Françoise, il allait chercher ou porter lui-même ses lettres ».
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's sustained observation stages Saint-Loup as wholly subjugated by an absent mistress who keeps him away, quarrels at a distance, and answers with delay or nonsense; his jealous hatred, his preemptive confession of unnamed faults, and his errands to the post office (paired with a servant's) present him as emotionally abased rather than merely unhappy.

appraisal_events.evidence: « je me sentis un peu irrité de cet enfantillage qui m'étonnait tellement de sa part. J'en arrivais même à me demander si je ne m'étais pas trompé sur ma grand'mère, si je ne la plaçais pas trop haut […] si elle n'avait pas ce que je croyais lui être le plus étranger, de la coquetterie. »
appraisal_events.explanation: Seeing his grandmother dress up and hesitate over hairstyles for Saint-Loup's photograph, the narrator lowers her from the pedestal of disinterested detachment on which he had kept her, suspecting childishness and vanity. The narrating voice frames this as his own possible error of judgment (« si je ne m'étais pas trompé »), so the diminishment is reported as the young narrator's suspicion rather than affirmed as true.

status_effects.explanation: He loses all leverage locally: kept at a distance, quarreled with without stated cause, and reduced to suffering, jealousy, and pleading for explanations.
His letters and telegrams go unanswered or receive replies « dénuées de sens », and his grief makes him concede guilt for a charge never formulated, so his speech carries no force.

In the narrator's local estimation she drops from an exceptionally high, self-detached standing to suspected coquetry and childishness, though the narration marks this as a suspicion he may have to revise.

ambiguities: The woman who dominates Saint-Loup is named nowhere in the passage (« son amie », « sa maîtresse »); she is not a reviewed unnamed figure on the reference sheet, so she is excluded from characters_present and the diminishment is recorded as narrator-framed rather than as a snub sourced to her.

The grandmother's diminishment is reported by the older narrating voice as a doubt his younger self entertained (« si je ne m'étais pas trompé sur ma grand'mère »); the text does not settle whether the mature narrator endorses the suspicion of coquetry or exposes it as a misreading, and the reading here takes the framing as ironizing distance.
